REBUILD-class for enabled — flake.nix bakes the supervisor block, so flipping it only takes effect after ./agentbox.sh rebuild. The schedules, interval, topic threshold, budget, weekly_window and repos are read at boot by the wrapper and on every run by skills/sealmap-review/scripts/review-cadence.cjs (a restart applies them; no rebuild). Every run, refusals included, appends one line to <repo>/docs/diagrams/review-ledger.jsonl; findings go to <repo>/docs/review/ as unverified hypotheses. features.jev_checkpoints.name: Jev checkpoints (timing judge for the advisor)
features.jev_checkpoints.summary: ADR-2135: the jev-checkpoints Claude Code function-hook plugin (config/claude-plugins/jev-checkpoints, authored in this repo) uses Jev (TypeSafe System One) as a cheap TIMING judge for when the Opus advisor of ADR-2134 is worth consulting. It injects at most one advisory line of 300 characters per checkpoint per turn and never forces a tool call. Four checkpoints, each switchable: done (a turn claims completion with no verifying run; Jev Score >= done_threshold), repeat (the same failure fingerprint recurs repeat_count times; LOCAL, never calls Jev), plan (a prompt needs a multi-file plan or touches an auth/schema/API/data contract; Score >= plan_threshold) and spawn (Jev Choice over haiku|sonnet|opus|inherit for a subagent; spawn_mode defaults to SHADOW, recording a decision log for ADR-2110 teacher labels, because the published codex-jev-router result found Jev-picked subagent models 69.7% dearer than one strong agent). Egress widens ADR-2090 as ADR-2121 did: prompt text, assistant final text and subagent prompt heads (clamped), plus a tool-call list (name, ok|error, first line of a Bash command), never tool-result contents. Email taint fence, sticky per session: an email-gateway/Gmail call or email-search load stops cloud requests for the rest of the session (a backend is local only when declared via backendLocal from the sovereign config, ADR-2094 §5). Fail-open: no key (TYPESAFE_API_KEY), timeout, 429 or any error injects nothing. Switch: /jev-checkpoints [status|on|off]. REBUILD-class: the plugin is gated in flake.nix; the entrypoint then sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS, registers the `agentbox` marketplace and installs jev-checkpoints@agentbox with the manifest as userConfig; false uninstalls (the shared switch and marketplace stay while factrail or ruflo-console is on). Needs Claude Code >= 2.1.294.

features.jev_compaction.name: Jev compaction with fact rails (factrail)
features.jev_compaction.summary: ADR-2093, implemented by ADR-2121: the factrail Claude Code function-hook plugin and Rust binary (DreamLab-AI/factrail, baked from one pinned commit by lib/factrail.nix as config/claude-plugins/factrail and /opt/agentbox/bin/factrail) replace the compaction SUMMARY with Jev decisions per tool call; what Jev lets go is REDUCED by fact rails, not deleted: a reproducible read becomes a note to re-run it, any other result keeps its head, fact lines and tail, and its full output is saved (secrets masked) with the path in the note. User and assistant text is never rewritten; tool-result contents never leave (only ok|error and a size). The cut is sized from the real context (aim 5/6 of the trigger, the fixed prefix counted; oldest outputs evicted to get under it); min_reduction_ratio is retired. Email taint fence, sticky per session: a session that has ever made an mcp__email-gateway__* / Gmail call or loaded email-search is never sent to a cloud judge and is compacted on local fact rails instead (fallback = "rules"), or judged when the backend is declared local (ADR-2094, ok-local). Switch: /factrail on|off|status; the old /jev-compact store (taints and switch) is migrated at boot. Without a key or on judge failure: fallback "rules" (local) or "summary" (built-in). Trigger min(compact_at_percent of the window, compact_at_tokens) with rearm_tokens hysteresis; cache_warm compacts an idle session above cache_warm_floor_tokens before its prompt cache expires. REBUILD-class: the binary and plugin are gated in flake.nix; the entrypoint then sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS, registers the `agentbox` marketplace and installs factrail@agentbox with the manifest as userConfig; false uninstalls and retracts. Needs Claude Code >= 2.1.274. Egress widened from ADR-2090 by operator decision with the email carve-out.

features.sovereign_system_one.name: Sovereign System One (local typed decisions)
features.sovereign_system_one.summary: ADR-2094: repoints BOTH System One consumers (the live skill router, ADR-2091, and Jev verbatim compaction, ADR-2093) from api.typesafe.ai at a LAN sidecar — system-one-facade on systemone:8097 over a loopback-only laya engine (services/laya-engine, open weights, Apache-2.0). The façade absorbs the capacity gap the cloud never had: option shortlisting (embedding-ranked top shortlist_k, always retaining none/other) and state windowing (top window_k), then re-expands so the answer names one of the CALLER'S original options with probability mass over ALL of them. BOOT-class HERE: the entrypoint runs `agentbox-manifest sso-project` and projects AGENTBOX_SKILL_ROUTE_API/_MODEL into runtime-env.sh and the router hook, plus baseUrl/model/backendLocal into the jev-compaction plugin userConfig — a flip applies on container restart and needs no image rebuild. The SIDECAR is a separate lifecycle (./agentbox.sh systemone up, docker-compose.system-one.yml, GPU, ~1.7 GB of weights on a named volume); enabling the gate without the sidecar running leaves the consumers failing open to their built-in paths. Disabled ⇒ NOTHING is projected and the cloud path is byte-identical (ADR-2020). An endpoint that is not LAN/loopback is REFUSED, not projected (E075), and the email taint fence keys off the explicit backendLocal boolean, never off the URL (ADR-2094 §5). Validator: E075/W073; W071/W072 stand down when this gate is on because TYPESAFE_API_KEY is no longer on the path.

skills.routing.cascade.summary: ADR-2095 addendum: a BM25 ranker over the skill rubrics answers a routing turn in-process when its relative top-two margin reaches [skills.routing].cascade_cutoff (default 0.3718); only the rest escalate to the judge. Off by default; boot inlines the variables into the hook command and runtime-env.sh only when on, so off is byte-identical. The JS ranker is held to system-one-eval by tests/system-one/cascade-parity. Validator E076.

skills.routing.label_log.name: Routing teacher labels (PROPOSED)

Email-gateway turns are never embedded; an off-LAN embeddings URL is refused (E077). Off until the ADR is accepted: storing prompt embeddings changes the ADR-2090 retention contract. Boot registration is byte-identical when off.

skills.routing.router.name: Live skill router (System One / Jev)
skills.routing.router.summary: ADR-2091: [skills.routing].router="jev" registers config/hooks/skill-route.cjs on UserPromptSubmit — one Choice over the REGISTERED skill descriptions per turn (ADR-2111; /route still ranks every routable skill), pick injected as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext — and /route (skills/skill-router/scripts/route.mjs) uses the same library. FAILS OPEN to router="table" (the pre-2091 path: always-loaded descriptions + routing-table.md) on any error, timeout, 429/529, missing TYPESAFE_API_KEY or a `none` pick. Egress of the routing prompt is accepted for skill routing only (ADR-2090). BOOT-class: the entrypoint inlines model/timeout/min-chars into the hook command and runtime-env.sh; router="table" or hook=false retracts the registration on the next boot (byte-identical-when-off). No image change on either value. cascade=true (ADR-2095 addendum, default off) answers turns whose local BM25 margin reaches cascade_cutoff in-process and escalates only the rest to the judge. label_log=true (ADR-2110, proposed, default off) registers config/hooks/routing-label-recorder.cjs on Stop to record per-turn teacher labels (prompt embedding, skills the main model used, router pick) into routing_labels — never prompt text, LAN-only embeddings, email turns excluded.

system_one.name: System One vendor slot (typed-decision proxy)
system_one.summary: ADR-2139: the System One judge is a vendor slot. [program:system-one-proxy] (crates/system-one/system-one-proxy, loopback [system_one].bind, default 127.0.0.1:8094) fronts all three typed-decision consumers (the live skill router ADR-2091, factrail compaction ADR-2121, the advisor checkpoints ADR-2135) and forwards POST /v1/systemone to the backend named by [system_one].backend out of [system_one.backends.*] (shipped: typesafe = Jev, subq = SubQ Snap, laya = the ADR-2094 facade sidecar, kev = a local Kev-9B server). The proxy owns the vendor keys (read from each backend's key_env, sent only to that key's hard-coded host over https, never to a local backend, redirects off), overwrites `model` with the backend's own and drops the Authorization a consumer sent. BOOT-class projection: the entrypoint runs `agentbox-manifest system-one-project`, writes /run/agentbox/system-one.json (the proxy's only config; re-read on change) and projects the proxy URL, the selected model and backendLocal = the selected backend's declared locality into runtime-env.sh, the router hook and both plugins' userConfig. LIVE subset: `./agentbox.sh systemone backend <name>` re-projects the JSON in place and the next request follows it — allowed between two backends of one locality class and from cloud to local; local-to-cloud is refused (and the proxy answers 503 backend_locality_changed) until the container restarts, because the consumers' email fence was projected at boot (ADR-2094 §5). The program itself is REBUILD-class (flake.nix bakes it from the in-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with [features.sovereign_system_one].enabled (E081). Observability: GET /v1/backend (active backend, per-backend counters, estimated spend) and the JSONL request log at [system_one].log (never content). Validator: E080/E081/W076; W071/W072 stand down because the vendor key lives in the proxy — the consumers still need TYPESAFE_API_KEY or FACTRAIL_API_KEY present as their own gate token.

vault.cli.name: Vault corpus CLI (the one door to the corpus)
vault.cli.summary: ADR-2107/ADR-2108: [vault].cli = true bakes the `vault` corpus CLI (crates/vault) into the Nix package set at /opt/agentbox/bin/vault; agents reach the corpus through it and the Loom over HTTP since the ontology-bridge MCP server was retired, so false leaves agents with no door. REBUILD-class — the package set is resolved at image composition; boot Phase 5d runs `vault --version` as the liveness half of the gate.

vault.format.name: Authored corpus (vault)
vault.format.summary: ADR-2028: [vault].root/pages/format are the single path authority for the authored corpus. The entrypoint reads them at boot and exports VAULT_ROOT/VAULT_PAGES/VAULT_FORMAT to every supervised program and tmux window; resolved values are in the top-level `vault` block of this view.

vault.loom_sync.name: HP Loom reconcile (vault -> served generation)
vault.loom_sync.summary: ADR-2140: every boot runs scripts/hp-loom-reconcile.sh in the background. check compares the committed vault HEAD with the generation the HP Loom serves; full also builds HEAD from a clean worktree, promotes and verifies it, pushes it to the HP and starts the HP's verifying reload. Fail-open; result in ~/.local/state/agentbox/hp-loom-reconcile.json. BOOT-class: read at start, no rebuild.

vault.tui.name: Vault TUI (Rune, tmux window 9 "Notes")

[voicelink].enabled bakes voice-paned from lib/voice-paned.nix; REBUILD-class. The ADR-044 cockpit and [voice] are unchanged.

voicelink.record_events.name: Voicelink event-spool hooks
voicelink.record_events.summary: ADR-2151: with [voicelink].enabled and record_events, Claude Code Stop and Notification hooks (root session and every profile) and the Codex notify program call `voice-paned record`, appending to ~/.local/state/voicelink/events.jsonl. Registered at boot by the entrypoint and agentbox-manifest provision-stacks; fail-open, nothing on stdout. BOOT-class.
